summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout planning: canary strategy, cutover timing, monitoring runbooks, SLOs, and security sign-offs. Agreed next steps for runbook delivery, traffic plan, and final pricing for Dedicated capacity. Customer requested a short canary window with rollback criteria and detailed alert mappings.
transcript:
[00:00] Dan Rivera (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — good morning, good afternoon. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Alex Chen (ClearGuide): Alex here.
[00:07] Rita Gomez (SRE): Rita.
[00:09] Tom Wallace (Product): Tom on.
[00:11] Nina Patel (Security): Nina here.
[00:13] Priya Shah (Redwood SE): Priya here.
[00:15] Maya Lopez (CSM): Maya here.
[00:18] Dan: Awesome. Agenda — quick status on POC results, then main chunk — rollout/cutover plan: canary, A/B, monitoring, runbooks, and open items.
[00:30] Tom: Quick status: the model latency and quality numbers look good on Redwood hosted; cost is roughly within our expected band but we still need final numbers for Dedicated. We ran the sample traffic for the past 48 hours.
[00:45] Priya: Right — small caveat notes in the spreadsheet — at 8k token sequences we saw tail latency spikes on the hosted pool, but with prefix caching enabled across sessions those spikes went down 30-40%. Also when we applied the batching profiles we recommended throughput improved without impacting p95 much.
[01:05] Alex: Sounds good. For rollout we're thinking low-risk: small canary to 5% traffic for 24 hours then step to 25% if metrics look green, then full cutover overnight on a weekend.
[01:20] Rita: The SRE concern is rolling back quickly — we need a documented rollback path and automated traffic switch. How fast can you flip routing?
[01:30] Priya: Routing flip is immediate in Redwood Console — we can redirect traffic to the previous model variant or to a fallback region, that usually is sub-1min for routing change but of course depends on in-flight requests. We'll provide the runbook steps including the API calls and UI steps.
[01:50] Nina: On security — we still need confirmation on KMS integration and audit log retention for Dedicated. Our compliance team requires 365-day audit logs and customer-managed keys.
[02:05] Dan: Noted. Dedicated supports KMS/HSM options; I'll attach the compliance sheet. Priya, can you confirm log retention options?
[02:12] Priya: Yes, Dedicated has configurable audit retention; default is 90 days but enterprise add-on supports 365. KMS is supported, and we can do a key rotation plan. I'll include the exact API endpoints and admin roles in the runbook.
[02:30] Tom: Back to canary length — Alex proposed 24 hours; are you comfortable with 24 vs 72? Our thought is 24 is sufficient if we have the right coverage of alerting.
[02:45] Rita: 24 might be okay but depends on user patterns — we need synthetic checks for peak intervals and a couple real-user metrics: error rate, latency p50/p95/p99, model quality regressions (we'll use sample prompts). If any of those breach thresholds, we must auto rollback.
[03:05] Priya: For quality monitoring we recommend hooking Redwood's eval probe; we can push a daily sample set and flag semantic regressions. We also support webhooks to fire into your SRE alerts.
[03:25] Alex: Can you show the canary dashboard config?
[03:30] Priya: Sure, I'll paste the dashboard template after this meeting — it includes panels for token throughput, latency histograms, error rates, cost burn, and a model-quality probe with expected similarity scores.
[03:50] Dan: Let's talk step-by-step cutover plan — propose: pre-cutover checklist (backups, sync config, stakeholders paged), canary (5% for 24h), evaluate metrics, expand to 25% for 6h, expand to 50% for 3h, then full 100% overnight. Any objections?
[04:15] Alex: No objections but prefer an A/B cohort split for the 25% stage to compare quality directly vs control.
[04:22] Tom: Agree on A/B for a subset of users. Also we need to coordinate with legal for announcement windows.
[04:30] Nina: Security signoff required before canary start — I'll need the KMS attestation and the audit log retention confirmation. Otherwise legal won't sign off.
[04:45] Dan: We'll deliver those docs this week.
[04:50] Priya: On rollback criteria — propose automatic rollback triggers: p95 latency increases > 40% vs baseline, error rate > 1% absolute, semantic regression score drop > 0.06 on our probe, and any high-severity security alerts.
[05:10] Rita: Need to be specific on window and evaluation period — for p95 spike, do we consider a 5-minute window with sustained breach or a 30-minute window?
[05:20] Priya: Good point — suggest 10-minute sustained breach for latency and a 30-minute window for quality probe to avoid noisy flips.
[05:30] Alex: Are there any rate-limiting or quota changes during canary? We need to make sure throttling doesn't skew metrics.
[05:40] Priya: We can pin model slots and rate limits per route for the canary. Also we can mirror traffic so you can run offline comparisons.
[05:50] Tom: How about load — if we hit autoscale thresholds on Dedicated will that cause cost surprise?
[05:55] Dan: For Dedicated we can set reserve capacity levels and autoscale policies. Pricing options include burst capacity tiers; I'll include estimated cost delta for the canary and 25/50% stages.
[06:10] Nina: Quick security question — are logs ever traversing Redwood-managed KMS when using customer-managed keys? We need to ensure control.
[06:18] Priya: With customer-managed keys, logs are encrypted under your key at rest; Redwood does not hold the key. We can also provide key usage reports.
[06:28] Rita: For monitoring integration — we want Prometheus metrics and Alertmanager hooks; can Redwood export the same metrics or do we rely on webhooks only?
[06:38] Priya: We support both: metric exporters for Prometheus and push/webhook integrations. The exporter exposes per-route token/sec, p50/p95/p99, error counters, and KV hit/miss rates.
[06:55] Alex: Great. For the runbook, include exact alert names mapping — e.g., Redwood.latency.p95, Redwood.errors.rate.
[07:04] Priya: Yup, will include mapping table.
[07:10] Dan: Anything else on rollbacks?
[07:15] Tom: Just ensure a clear communication plan: who pages who, escalation path, and timeline to revert.
[07:23] Maya: I'll draft the communication template — e.g., 1) SRE triage 2) call stakeholders 3) execute rollback — with Slack and PagerDuty snippets.
[07:34] Alex: On A/B, how do we tag cohorts? We prefer user-id hashing to split deterministic cohorts so we can re-run analysis.
[07:42] Priya: Use the route parameter with hash-based splitting — Redwood supports stable cohorts so you won't get leakage.
[07:50] Rita: One more — data residency: some EU traffic must remain in EU region. We need region-aware routing during canary.
[07:58] Priya: That's supported; we can pin EU traffic to EU region and only run canary in EU for that subset. Noted for runbook.
[08:10] Alex: Ok timeline — we want to start canary next Friday, 2026-04-30 at 02:00 UTC. Is that doable?
[08:18] Dan: Yes, provided docs and runbooks delivered by Wednesday EOD and we have sign-off from security.
[08:25] Nina: Security turnaround — if you send the KMS and audit docs by Wednesday we can aim to sign off by Thursday.
[08:33] Dan: Action: Priya share runbook & dashboard links by 2026-04-26; Dan send Dedicated pricing and SLA by 2026-04-25; Alex finalize traffic plan by 2026-04-28.
[08:45] Tom: Also request a short smoke benchmark right before canary at canary scale — maybe a 30-minute synthetic run to validate telemetry.
[08:55] Priya: We can schedule a smoke test the morning of the canary — we'll send the script and run with you.
[09:05] Alex: On cost monitoring — can Redwood stream per-route cost burn rates so product can see real-time projected cost during canary?
[09:14] Priya: Yes, cost panels are available and we can export burn rate to your billing dashboards. We'll include recommended budget alert thresholds.
[09:28] Dan: Anything else?
[09:32] Rita: Just one small nit — the transcript of earlier POC had a couple misattributed speakers, be careful on the recorded attendee list.
[09:40] Maya: Noted — we'll attach the recording and cleaned attendee list to the notes.
[09:46] Dan: Great — recap of next steps and we'll sync mid-week if any blockers. Thanks everyone.
[09:55] Alex: Thanks.
[09:56] Tom: Thanks.
[09:57] Nina: Bye.
[09:58] Priya: Bye.
[09:59] Maya: Bye.

Notes: audio transcription had some minor name errors. Shared artifacts: linked runbook template (link: https://redwood.example/runbooks/canary-template), POC benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.example/poctools/clearguide-bench.xlsx), Dedicated pricing deck (link: https://redwood.example/pricing/dedicated.pdf).
